record.proposal_text:
PROPOSAL SUMMARY:
This technical proposal from Cortech Consulting Group responds to ICPAC's RFP to design and pilot community-based anticipatory action systems in Mandera and Moyale. Cortech positions itself as an international development consulting firm with 10+ years of experience in East Africa, particularly in fragile and humanitarian contexts. The proposal demonstrates distinctive organizational capacity through multidisciplinary technical platforms (MEAL, climate resilience, early warning systems, GIS), a decentralized field-delivery model balancing centralized oversight with localized engagement, and proven experience with similar assignments in the target regions. The firm emphasizes six operational principles—contextual intelligence, technical rigor, participation, actionability, innovation, and results accountability—as particularly relevant to building locally-understood, institutionally-owned anticipatory action systems. Cortech leverages relevant recent experience including a WASH in Emergency Anticipatory Action assignment in Moyale and Mandera (2025) and demonstrates institutional credibility through ISO certifications and compliance across relevant jurisdictions.

METHODOLOGY:
The approach combines participatory stakeholder engagement, secondary-data analysis, and risk/vulnerability assessment to design Early Action Plans (EAPs) and Anticipatory Action Plans (AAPs). The methodology integrates technical analysis with community-based participation, institutional assessment, cross-border programming expertise, and GIS/data management capabilities to ensure interventions are technically credible, operationally feasible, and socially inclusive.

WRITING STYLE:
The proposal uses formal, compliance-oriented language in the cover declaration (Form TECH-1) with structured checkboxes addressing World Bank policies and fraud/corruption requirements. The technical narrative (Form TECH-2) shifts to professional third-person exposition emphasizing organizational capabilities, demonstrated experience, and technical credentials. Writing style is evidence-based, citing specific past projects and outcomes with references; uses numbered subsections and parallel structure for readability; avoids excessive jargon but maintains technical specificity (e.g., 'EAP/AAP', 'GEDSI', 'MEAL'); and balances institutional positioning with concrete operational detail.

KEY SECTIONS:
Proposal Submission Cover (Form TECH-1), Consultant's Organization and Experience (Form TECH-2), Background and Organizational Profile, Organizational Capacity Relevant to the Assignment, Organizational Structure for the Assignment, Organizational Chart, Board of Directors and Beneficial Ownership, Selected Relevant Corporate Experience, Direct Relevance of Moyale and Mandera Experience, Key Expert Profiles and CVs, SEA/SH Declaration

Consultant’s Organization and Experience
A. CONSULTANT’S ORGANIZATION
A.1 Background and Organizational Profile
Cortech Consulting Group is an international development consulting firm established in 2015, with over ten years of experience providing technical consulting, research, monitoring and evaluation, institutional strengthening and advisory services to governments, international organizations, humanitarian agencies, development partners, NGOs, CSOs and private-sector actors across East Africa and other African countries. The firm has successfully implemented assignments in Kenya, Somalia, Ethiopia, Djibouti, Sudan, South Sudan, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe, with particularly strong operational experience in fragile, humanitarian and institutionally complex environments.
Cortech's technical platform spans monitoring, evaluation and learning; third-party monitoring; impact assessment; context and needs analysis; data collection and analysis; resilience and livelihoods; agriculture and food systems; emergency response; climate change; migration management; WASH; protection; infrastructure; governance; and social and environmental assessment. This multidisciplinary capability enables the firm to address complex assignments that require integration of technical analysis, stakeholder engagement, field-based evidence, institutional assessment and practical implementation planning.
For the present assignment, Cortech brings particularly relevant institutional and technical capabilities in community-based early warning and disaster risk reduction, climate and resilience programming, vulnerability and needs assessment, participatory stakeholder engagement, cross-border and regional programming, MEAL, GEDSI, data management and evidence-to-action programming. The firm's recent experience includes a Community Early Warning and Disaster Risk Reduction Training Support assignment in Somalia involving hazard and vulnerability assessment, review of early warning systems, community linkages and training needs assessment.
Cortech has also undertaken assignments involving institutional assessment, governance analysis, stakeholder consultation, capacity development and operational recommendations. Its work with the World Bank, IGAD, UN agencies, international NGOs and government institutions demonstrates its ability to work across complex institutional environments and translate evidence into practical recommendations and systems improvements.
The firm's delivery model is founded on six principles: contextual intelligence, technical rigour, participation and ownership, actionability, innovation, and results and accountability. These principles are particularly relevant to the proposed Community-Based Anticipatory Action Pilot because the assignment requires more than technical risk analysis; it requires an operational system that is locally understood, institutionally owned, inclusive, practical and capable of translating early warning information into timely anticipatory action. Cortech has engaged more than 60 local and international organizations and has successfully completed more than 45 projects across Somalia, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan and Zimbabwe. Its experience includes large-scale field data collection, participatory research, mixed-methods assessments, GEDSI assessments, monitoring frameworks and strategic knowledge products.
Cortech Consulting Group Ltd is legally registered, licensed, and operationally compliant across all jurisdictions relevant to this assignment (See Annex II for relevant registration certificates). The firm holds ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management), ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational Health and Safety) certifications, issued July 2025 and valid to July 2028.
A.2 Organizational Capacity Relevant to the Assignment
Cortech will deploy its organizational resources through an integrated technical and project-management structure capable of supporting the full assignment cycle, from inception and secondary-data analysis through risk and vulnerability assessment, participatory stakeholder engagement, trigger development, EAP/AAP design, pilot activation, MEAL, learning and institutionalization. The firm will combine senior technical leadership with specialist expertise in anticipatory action and disaster risk reduction, climate and early warning systems, cross-border programming, MEAL, GIS and data management, GEDSI, safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and community engagement. This multidisciplinary configuration will ensure that the proposed EAP/AAPs are simultaneously technically credible, operationally feasible, socially inclusive and appropriate to the institutional realities of Mandera and Moyale.
Cortech's organizational approach is based on maintaining centralized technical oversight while deploying field resources close to the communities and institutions with which the assignment will engage. This will allow the firm to maintain consistency across the two IGAD clusters while accommodating the distinct social, institutional, livelihood, security and cross-border characteristics of Mandera and Moyale. The firm's technology-oriented capabilities further include digital data collection, dashboards, data migration, information management and cybersecurity risk assessment, providing an appropriate platform for the assignment's requirements concerning secure data collection, risk monitoring, trigger tracking, GIS analysis, reporting and knowledge management.
A.3 Organizational Structure for the Assignment
For purposes of this assignment, Cortech will operate through a Team Leader-led multidisciplinary structure, supported by specialized technical leads and field implementation personnel.
This structure will facilitate vertical accountability and horizontal technical integration. The Team Leader will provide the principal interface with ICPAC, while technical specialists will lead their respective workstreams and contribute to integrated outputs.
A.4 Organizational Chart for the Assignment
A.5 Board of Directors and Beneficial Ownership
B. CONSULTANT’S EXPERIENCE
B.1 Selected Relevant Corporate Experience
B.2 Direct Relevance of the Moyale and Mandera Experience
The WASH in Emergency Anticipatory Action assignment in Moyale and Mandera Counties is just one of Cortech's most directly comparable corporate assignment for the present consultancy. Implemented for the Danish Refugee Council between April and June 2025, the assignment involved delivery of WASH interventions within an emergency anticipatory action framework in the same two counties that constitute the Kenyan geographic focus of the proposed pilot. The assignment therefore provides Cortech with direct operational familiarity with the local context, community structures, WASH vulnerabilities and practical requirements associated with delivering anticipatory interventions in Moyale and Mandera. The assignment also demonstrates Cortech's ability to translate anticipatory action principles into concrete, community-level interventions. The combination of WASH needs assessment, emergency water supply support, hygiene promotion and strengthening of community-based WASH structures is particularly relevant to the proposed consultancy because it demonstrates experience moving from assessment and risk identification to practical action and community-level preparedness.
The Community Early Warning and DRR assignment is particularly strong evidence of Cortech's direct relevance to this RFP because its scope included hazard and vulnerability assessment, review of early warning systems, community linkages and DRR capacity development, within a fragile and hazard-prone East African operating environment. The IGAD land governance evaluation provides additional evidence of Cortech's ability to operate at regional and IGAD institutional level, undertake forward-looking analysis and generate evidence to support sustainability and future programming. The Kenya Agritech assignment demonstrates Cortech's capacity to undertake stakeholder mapping, field-based data collection, ecosystem analysis and actionable programme design, including engagement with government institutions, communities, market actors and other stakeholders. The World Bank institutional capacity assignment demonstrates the firm's ability to undertake complex institutional assessments involving stakeholder interviews, policy analysis, identification of governance constraints and development of practical capacity-strengthening recommendations. This experience will allow Cortech to approach the present assignment with an understanding of the operational realities of the two counties, while ensuring that the proposed cross-border EAP/AAPs are informed by actual implementation experience rather than solely by desk-based analysis.
Research, Learning and Resilience Experience in Mandera
Cortech's Pathways to Prosperity (P2P) Research and Learning assignment in Mandera and Turkana Counties further strengthens the firm's contextual experience in northern Kenya. Implemented for the Danish Refugee Council in January–February 2023, the assignment focused on generating evidence to inform inclusive economic growth and resilience-building interventions. This experience is relevant to the present assignment because effective anticipatory action requires an understanding of how hazards affect household livelihoods, economic security, vulnerability and resilience. Cortech's research and learning experience in Mandera therefore complements its direct anticipatory WASH implementation experience and strengthens its ability to connect risk analysis with livelihood and resilience outcomes.
Combined Relevance to the Present Assignment
Taken together, these assignments provide Cortech with an unusually strong combination of location-specific, thematic and operational experience. The firm's WASH Anticipatory Action assignment provides direct experience in both Moyale and Mandera and specifically involved emergency anticipatory action. The P2P Research and Learning assignment provides additional Mandera-specific experience in resilience and evidence generation. The Somalia Community Early Warning and DRR assignment provides directly relevant experience in hazard and vulnerability assessment, early warning systems and community-level DRR. The IGAD assignment provides regional institutional experience, while Cortech's broader Kenya and East Africa portfolio provides the field implementation, MEAL, stakeholder engagement and analytical capabilities required to translate these experiences into a harmonized cross-border model. This combination positions Cortech to contribute not only technical expertise but also practical contextual intelligence on the communities and operating environment in which the pilot will be implemented.
B.3 Regional and IGAD Experience
Cortech's corporate experience is not limited to individual country assignments. The firm has demonstrated experience working within IGAD regional structures and multi-country East African environments. In 2026, Cortech completed the end-of-project evaluation of the Improving Land Governance in the IGAD Region Programme (Phase II) for IGAD/Swedish Embassy in Ethiopia. The assignment covered the full implementation period from 2023 to 2026 and assessed project design, implementation, performance, lessons learned, institutional capacity, sustainability and future programming implications.
